rationale: B wins narrowly because it most consistently translates the product authority into a full-surface implementation contract: next-hour exceptions lead; historical and diagnostic information is demoted; retained KPIs gain thresholds and semantic meaning; impact alignment, textual statuses, explicit actions, actionable insights, contrast, spacing, elevation, focus, responsive sizes, and operational states all receive observable treatment. C is an exceptionally close second with stronger first-viewport measurability in places, while A is also excellent but leaves the generic insight content less explicitly resolved.

results.label: A
results.summary: A correctly recenters the surface on the next-hour exception queue and provides especially measurable first-viewport, row-content, status, action, and edge-case acceptance criteria. Its main gap is that the redesign moves flatten the nested insight area without explicitly removing or operationalizing the generic insight copy; its typography, contrast, and spacing corrections are also less testable than its table criteria.

results.label: B
results.summary: B is the most complete and economical response: it establishes the exception queue as the lead surface, tiers operational versus diagnostic metrics, converts vague insights into threshold-and-action content linked to the table, and covers typography, semantic color, alignment, spacing, elevation, keyboard focus, responsive behavior, and failure states. A few acceptance phrases such as “visually secondary” and “readable dense-table role” remain less measurable than ideal.

results.label: C
results.summary: C offers a highly coherent urgency-first hierarchy, explicit first-viewport row capacity, strong product-identity handling, a useful global-header correction, and a clear rule that every secondary module must help prioritize exceptions. It is slightly behind B because its typography, contrast, spacing, elevation, and responsive-state acceptance criteria are less fully specified, while example actions such as “Snooze” and “Fix” are somewhat more speculative relative to the supplied workflows.
